top_level_objectives: Represent physical quantities using vectors with magnitude and direction.
Add vectors graphically and interpret the resultant vector.
Resolve a vector into horizontal and vertical components using right-triangle relationships.
Apply vector components to analyze projectile motion in two dimensions.
Explain the independence of horizontal and vertical motion in ideal projectile motion.
Predict how launch speed and launch angle affect range, maximum height, and trajectory shape.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 1: Vectors as Arrows in Space
scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce vectors as quantities with both magnitude and direction, distinct from scalars.
key_visuals: A floating 2D coordinate grid anchored on the tabletop or floor
Several colored arrows of different lengths and directions
Labels showing magnitude, direction angle, and units
student_actions: Inspect and compare arrows with different magnitudes and directions.
Adjust one vector’s length and angle and observe the changing magnitude and direction labels.
Identify which displayed quantities are vectors and which are scalars.

scenes.brief_purpose: Show how two displacement or velocity vectors combine graphically to form a resultant.
key_visuals: Two draggable arrows placed on a grid
A ghosted tip-to-tail copy of the second vector
A highlighted resultant arrow from the first tail to the final tip
Numerical readouts for component sums and resultant magnitude
student_actions: Drag vectors into tip-to-tail arrangement.
Compare the resultant to the original two vectors.
Change vector directions and lengths to see how the resultant changes.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 3: Decomposing a Vector into Components
scenes.brief_purpose: Connect a single angled vector to perpendicular x- and y-components.
key_visuals: One launch-like arrow at an angle above the horizontal
Dashed horizontal and vertical component arrows forming a right triangle
Angle marker and labels for vector magnitude, x-component, and y-component
Simple trigonometry relationships displayed near the triangle
student_actions: Rotate and resize the vector and watch the component arrows update.
Use component labels to relate cosine to the horizontal component and sine to the vertical component.
Answer a short prompt predicting which component grows or shrinks as the angle changes.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 4: Initial Velocity of a Projectile
scenes.brief_purpose: Apply vector decomposition to the initial velocity of a launched projectile.
key_visuals: A small launcher on a flat ground plane
An initial velocity arrow emerging from the launcher
Separate horizontal and vertical velocity component arrows
Controls for launch speed and launch angle
student_actions: Set a launch speed and angle.
Observe the initial velocity vector split into horizontal and vertical components.
Predict whether changing angle at fixed speed affects horizontal speed, vertical speed, or both.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 5: Independent Horizontal and Vertical Motion
scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate that horizontal motion remains constant while vertical motion changes under gravity.
key_visuals: Projectile frozen at several time-stamped positions along a path
Equal horizontal spacing markers for equal time intervals
Vertical velocity arrows that shrink during ascent, vanish near the top, then point downward and grow
A constant horizontal velocity arrow repeated at each position
student_actions: Step through the projectile’s motion frame by frame.
Compare horizontal displacements during equal time intervals.
Observe and describe how the vertical velocity changes while horizontal velocity stays the same.

scenes.brief_purpose: Show that the curved path results from combining constant horizontal velocity with accelerated vertical motion.
key_visuals: Separate side panels showing horizontal position versus time and vertical position versus time
A combined 2D projectile trajectory in the main view
Falling-motion guide showing uniform downward acceleration
Trace dots forming a parabola
student_actions: Play the motion and compare the separate x and y motion displays with the combined trajectory.
Match time markers across the component views and the full path.
Explain why the path curves even though horizontal motion is uniform.

scenes.scene_name: Scene 7: Launch Angle and Speed Investigation
scenes.brief_purpose: Let students explore how initial speed and angle affect range, height, and time of flight.
key_visuals: Interactive launcher with adjustable angle and speed sliders
Multiple color-coded trajectory traces for different trials
Range marker on the ground and maximum-height marker above the arc
Data panel listing speed, angle, range, maximum height, and flight time
student_actions: Run several launches while varying one parameter at a time.
Compare trajectories at different launch angles for the same speed.
Record which settings produce greater range and which produce greater maximum height.

scenes.brief_purpose: Consolidate vector and projectile concepts through a target-hitting prediction task.
key_visuals: A target placed at a fixed horizontal distance and height
Launcher, initial velocity vector, and optional component hints
Predicted trajectory preview after student submits values
Final summary overlay linking vector components to projectile outcomes
student_actions: Choose a launch speed and angle to hit the target.
Justify the choice using horizontal and vertical components.
Launch the projectile, compare prediction to result, and revise if necessary.
